expectations.text: The title or first heading contains the emitted error text or its identifying substring, not a topic label such as 'Upload problems'
expectations.evidence: Title: "# `cache upload rejected (HTTP 413): object exceeds the per-object limit`" — directly lifted from the error string, not a generic label.

expectations.text: An applies-to section names CLI 2.1 through 2.8, Linux and macOS, and the `team` and `starter` plans, and states that `enterprise` is unaffected
expectations.evidence: "CLI 2.1 through current (2.8), on Linux and macOS." and "Plans `team` and `starter`... Plan `enterprise` has no per-object limit and cannot produce this error"

expectations.text: The fix branches into separate per-cause blocks rather than one flat list of every check
expectations.evidence: Three separate ### subsections: "If `TESSELLATE_MAX_OBJECT` is set above your plan's limit", "If the artifact really is over the limit", "If a corporate proxy is mangling the upload".

expectations.text: The 3-minute plan-limit check is ordered ahead of the instant `TESSELLATE_MAX_OBJECT` check
expectations.evidence: The `TESSELLATE_MAX_OBJECT` check ('a ten-second check') is listed first, and the artifact-size check ('takes a few minutes...run this after ruling out the free check above, not before') is listed second — the opposite of the order this item requires.

expectations.text: The ordering rationale is stated as how often that check is the actual cause per minute of the reader's time, explicitly not cheapest-check-first
expectations.evidence: Preamble states branches are "ordered by cause-likelihood ÷ diagnosis-time"; body reinforces with e.g. "Most common cause (roughly 7 in 10 cases), but confirming it takes a few minutes... run this after ruling out the free check above, not before" — likelihood weighed against time rather than pure cost.

expectations.text: The proxy-chunking cause is placed last as the successive fall-back
expectations.evidence: "### If a corporate proxy is mangling the upload... Rare (roughly 1 in 20 cases) and the slowest to confirm — only worth it once the two checks above have come back clean." is the third and final branch.

expectations.text: The words 'simply', 'easy' and 'just' do not appear describing the fix
expectations.evidence: No occurrence of 'simply' or 'easy'; the only 'just' occurrence — "Flagged as a product gap, not just a support scenario" — describes a classification, not a fix step.

expectations.text: No sentence attributes the failure to the reader forgetting or doing something wrong
expectations.evidence: Causes are framed as product/environment issues, e.g. "the client doesn't validate that before trying to upload" and "Flagged as a product gap, not just a support scenario" — no phrasing like 'you forgot' or 'your mistake'.

expectations.text: The confirmation part names a specific observable output or state rather than the absence of the error
expectations.evidence: "re-running `tessellate cache inspect --largest 10` no longer shows an object at or above your plan's limit (unless you upgraded plans, in which case it's expected to still be listed but no longer rejected)" — a concrete command output, not just 'no more error'.

expectations.text: The escape hatch names the specific artifacts to attach and a place to report, rather than a bare 'contact support'
expectations.evidence: "Open a support request with: CLI version..., Plan name..., Output of `echo $TESSELLATE_MAX_OBJECT`..., Output of `tessellate cache inspect --largest 10`..., ...`curl -v --trace-ascii` capture" plus "Never attach the artifact itself or full object contents".
